brief: Distinguish an unchanged money amount from its purchasing power when the same basket of goods becomes more expensive.

en-US.scenario: Fictional US-dollar examples for "What your money can buy"; illustrative amounts, not current prices or product offers. No assumption of salary, bank ownership or spare income.

es-MX.scenario: Ejemplos ficticios en pesos mexicanos para "Lo que compra tu dinero"; montos ilustrativos, no precios vigentes ni ofertas. No se supone nómina, cuenta bancaria ni dinero sobrante.

pt-BR.scenario: Exemplos fictícios em reais para "O que seu dinheiro compra"; valores ilustrativos, não preços atuais nem ofertas. Sem supor salário, conta bancária ou dinheiro sobrando.

objective.observable_action: Distinguish an unchanged money amount from its purchasing power when the same basket of goods becomes more expensive.
objective.success_criterion: Complete the fresh-context transfer using only its visible information.

instruction.relevance: Keeping the same amount of dollars does not always preserve what it buys. These price changes are fictional examples.
instruction.misconception: Assuming that a stable account balance guarantees the ability to buy the same goods later.
instruction.numeracy_support: Use a single stated percentage increase and compare the resulting basket price with unchanged cash.

evidence.reasoning: A basket costs 100 today and 110 later. Keeping 100 does not buy the same basket at the later price.
Purchasing power means what money can buy. Inflation is a general rise in prices; individual prices can change differently.
Fictional prices: compare 1% and 5% after one year. The graph spans two years.
The unchanged balance no longer covers the same basket.
The price increase is added to the original basket cost.
Purchasing power connects money with current goods prices.
One price change alone does not establish the general inflation rate.
A higher money amount can still fall short of the same basket.
The same reserved amount covers less of the unchanged repair.

delayed_retrieval.fresh_context: Apply this skill in a later integrated decision with a different constraint.

en-US.line: Keeping the same amount of dollars does not always preserve what it buys. These price changes are fictional examples.

es-MX.line: Conservar el mismo monto de pesos no siempre mantiene lo que compra. Estos cambios de precios son ejemplos ficticios.

pt-BR.line: Manter o mesmo valor em reais nem sempre preserva o que ele compra. Estas mudanças de preços são exemplos fictícios.

en-US.line: A basket costs 100 today and 110 later. Keeping 100 does not buy the same basket at the later price.

es-MX.line: Una canasta cuesta 100 hoy y 110 después. Conservar 100 no compra la misma canasta al precio posterior.

en-US.line: Purchasing power means what money can buy. Inflation is a general rise in prices; individual prices can change differently.

es-MX.line: El poder de compra es lo que compra el dinero. La inflación es un aumento general de precios; cada precio puede cambiar distinto.

pt-BR.line: Poder de compra é o que o dinheiro compra. Inflação é uma alta geral de preços; cada preço pode mudar de modo diferente.

en-US.prompt: Fictional prices: compare 1% and 5% after one year. The graph spans two years.

es-MX.prompt: Precios ficticios: compara 1% y 5% durante un año usando la tabla. La gráfica abarca dos años, no es un pronóstico.

pt-BR.prompt: Preços fictícios: compare 1% e 5% durante um ano usando a tabela. O gráfico abrange dois anos, não é previsão.
